blush-paper.$description: Blush Paper — Page canvas, all section backgrounds — the warm rose-tinted ground that gives the entire site its editorial, printed-on-paper feel. Never a flat white, never a cool gray

carbon-ink.$description: Carbon Ink — Primary text, filled buttons, all iconography, form labels, footer rules. The dominant non-canvas color — drives every typographic and interactive element

bone-white.$description: Bone White — Text color inside filled black buttons, reverse-fill surfaces, and form input contrast. Used sparingly as the counter-tone to Carbon Ink

fossil-gray.$description: Fossil Gray — Muted helper text, secondary metadata, subdued form placeholder tones. The only neutral that softens Carbon Ink for non-primary copy

signal-blue.$description: Signal Blue — Violet accent for outlined action borders, linked labels, and lightweight interactive emphasis.

copernicus.$description: Copernicus carries the entire voice — it is a high-contrast transitional serif whose terminals and sharp serifs make 70–90px display sizes feel literary rather than decorative. The signature move is its aggressive negative tracking: -0.092em at 90px tightens the headline into a near-solid mass of type, which against the warm blush ground reads as a printed editorial pull-quote, not a SaaS H1. Body sizes (15–18px) sit at near-normal tracking, so the tension between tight display and loose running text mirrors a magazine spread.

helvetica.$description: A vestigial system-font presence — appears only in minor utility spots (small labels, icons-in-text). Not a typographic voice; effectively a fallback safety net.
